sections.heading: Beginner Tips and Tricks
sections.body:
If you're new to 'Falling Cubes,' here are some beginner tips and tricks to help you get started:

1. Start with the easiest difficulty level and gradually increase the difficulty as you become more comfortable with the gameplay mechanics.

2. Focus on anticipating the next cube, rather than reacting to it. This will help you develop your spatial awareness and reaction time.

3. Use the edge of the screen to your advantage. The cubes tend to bounce off the edge, giving you a chance to dodge them or even use them to your advantage.

4. Experiment with different controls and settings to find what works best for you. You can use the mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to play the game, and you can also adjust the sensitivity and speed to suit your preferences.

5. Don't be afraid to fail. 'Falling Cubes' is a challenging game, and you'll inevitably fail at times. However, don't get discouraged - use your failures as an opportunity to learn and improve your gameplay.

sections.heading: Advanced Strategies
sections.body:
Once you've mastered the basics of 'Falling Cubes,' it's time to take your gameplay to the next level. Here are some advanced strategies to help you improve your skills:

1. Use the 'edge-dodge' technique. This involves using the edge of the screen to your advantage, bouncing the cubes off the edge to create a safe path or even using them to your advantage.

2. Anticipate the cube's trajectory. By analyzing the cube's speed, size, and direction, you can anticipate its trajectory and plan your next move accordingly.

3. Use the 'cube-combo' technique. This involves dodging multiple cubes in a row, creating a chain reaction that will give you a high score and a sense of accomplishment.

4. Experiment with different controls and settings. You can adjust the sensitivity and speed to suit your preferences, and you can also use the mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to play the game.

5. Practice, practice, practice. The more you play 'Falling Cubes,' the better you'll become at anticipating the cubes, developing your spatial awareness, and improving your reaction time.
